THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE 15

ASSOCIATION WITH THE REVEREND LEWIS HOLLAND

About the middle of the first school year (early in 1877), Mr. Halsel was joined in his labors, if modest, undertaking by one Lewis Holland, who is described as a well-established scholar, a minister of the Baptist Church, and a teacher of considerable experience. For a year these two men had led students together and at Ladonia College. For the ten years following 1877, Mr. Holland had been teaching and farming in the neighborhood of Whitewright.²³

Both the aforementioned men, who, for the next ten years were to work in fine harmony in building the small school in Savoy into a college, appear to have been most auspicious things. In personality and abilities each complement[ed] the other. Mr. Halsel, three years the younger, was of the more popular type, to receiving more immediate consideration and consideration. Mr. Holland was of the quieter, more reserved in nature, profoundly learned and perhaps the more to be commended consideration.

EXPANSION OF THE PLANT

As the school grew, the original one-roomed building was soon overcrowded; but at the time the school had not yet made for itself any sufficient grounds for expansion. The property is described in the deed from F. J. Abernathy to the school in 1882, then jointly owned by[?] being situated on the south side of and adjoining the town of Savoy,²⁴ being situated at about twelve by twelve by twelve square feet, containing about two and a half acres. A consideration of $1,701 is stated.

The first expansion was the addition of a one-roomed building known as "Mr. Holland's room."
